m.s: Heat a drizzle of oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook finely diced {onion} and {carrot} for 8 minutes until soft. Add crushed {garlic}, grated {ginger} and {currypowder} and stir for 1 minute.

Stir in {flour*0.5} for 1 minute, then whisk in {stockpowder} dissolved in ¾ cup hot water per serve. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then. Add {honey} and {soy}, then blitz smooth with a stick blender.

Rinse {rice} until the water runs clear. Put it in a saucepan with 1½ times its volume of cold water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes so it finishes steaming. Finely shred the cabbage and toss with {ricevinegar} and a pinch each of salt and sugar.
Flatten {chk_thigh} a little with your hand so they're an even thickness. Dust in the rest of the flour, dip in beaten {eggs}, then press firmly into {panko}.

Heat 1cm of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in batches for 4 minutes a side until deep golden and cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Drain on paper towel, rest for 2 minutes, then slice.
Plate the rice, chicken and slaw, and pour the curry sauce alongside so the crumb stays crunchy.

l: Keep the sauce separate and reheat the chicken in the oven or air fryer so it stays crunchy. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: GF flour in the sauce (make a small separate pot) and for crumbing, with GF crumbs. Tamari instead of soy. Fry the GF chicken first in fresh oil.
